newsitem.title: UK: Four MGAM directors quit in fund shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Four MGAM directors quit in fund shake-up.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank, on Wednesday announced the departure of four key managers following aprobe into irregularities in its unit trust business.
It also named Robert Smith as the group's asset management head, replacing Keith Percy as chief executive of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
Four MGAM directors quit in fund shake-up =2

Percy, along with directors Glyn Owen, Graham Kane and Michael Wheatley will all leave the firm following a probe into irregularities in its unit trust investment funds which were managed by Peter Young, now suspended, DMG said in a statement.

"Our internal investigations have revealed management failings which contributed to the problems in our unit trust business and these changes have been made as a result," DMG chief executive Michael Dobson said.

Their departures follow revelations of major problems in three MGAM funds last month. The discovery of misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to the temporary suspension of the funds and a 180 million pound ($284.9 million) cash injection by Deutsche Bank to shore them up.
Young, who is currently being investigated by Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) has said he is not guilty of any criminal activity and is being made a scapegoat for failings.
